specs.note: AC supply hot at all times, no switch

steps: Unpack & check the packet

Unpack the fireplace and open the manual packet: glass latch tool #HA-77-00256, remote #HA-110-00105 with 3 AAA batteries, backup battery holder with 4 AA batteries, backup power harness #10-03-00128 and the manual, all of which stay with the homeowner. Log set, firebox lining and decorative front are bought separately.
Frame, place & level

Frame the chase to at least 40-5/8" W × 40-3/4" H × 14-5/8" D on a wood, masonry or metal floor. Unbolt the unit from its pallet, bend up the shipping clips, then set it in the chase, level and plumb, and secure it to the framing studs.

Minimum rough framing: 40-5/8" wide × 40 3/4" high × 14-5/8" deep, with a vent opening 10" high × 9" wide. On the left side, the ignition system box protrudes ½" and an electrical cable clamp 1-1/4".

  • Build the chase like the home's outside walls: insulate walls, ceiling, base plate and cantilever floor, fit vapor and air infiltration barriers, and seal fire stops, gas line holes and other openings with high temperature caulk.
  • On a cement slab, a layer of plywood under the unit may be used to stop cold conducting up into the room.
  • The four lifting handles (one each side, two on the rear wall) are for lifting and short moves only, never for carrying: remove one screw and pull the top section out. Net weight 220 lbs.; team lift recommended.
  • Mobile (manufactured) homes: bolt the unit to the floor and ground it.
  • Indoors only: fully protected from precipitation and excessive moisture, with the ambient temperature between 32°F and 110°F.
  • Before the hearth pad or wall finish goes on, make sure the finishing guides match the front being used. The factory bottom guide sits 1 1/2" above the bottom of the fireplace.
LP conversion (if needed)

To burn LP, install kit #HA-106-00023: 3/64" drilled orifices on both burners, the pilot NG/LP clip pushed in until "NAT" is hidden, and the motorized LP regulator on the gas valve. Mendota recommends converting before the fireplace goes into its framed cavity.

A qualified service agency must do this. Shut off the gas supply, then turn off the electrical supply.

  1. With a 1/4" hex driver, remove the 2 screws holding the rear and front burners to the burner airbox. Lift out the front burner, loosen its air shutter screw and open the shutter 1/4" minimum.
  2. Slide the rear burner about 2" to the right and lift it out.
  3. With a 1/2" deep well socket, remove the front and rear orifices. Thread a new 3/64" drilled orifice onto each fitting and tighten.
  4. Remove the left-side access panel and lay it down without disconnecting any wires.
  5. Pilot (right side of the firebox): hold the pilot base tightly with large vice grips, loosen the hex base 1/4 turn counterclockwise with a 7/16" open end wrench, push the NG/LP clip all the way in so "NAT" isn't visible, and retighten.
  6. Regulator: with the supplied Torx T20, remove and discard the two mounting screws, the regulator tower and the spring and diaphragm assembly. Check the rubber gasket, fit the stepper motor regulator with the provided M4 x 0.7 screws and tighten to 25lb-in, plus or minus 5. Stripped valve threads mean a new valve. Put the identification label on the valve body.

Then light the pilot: its flames must be at least 1" long and overlap the propagation ports on both burners. The burners must light immediately without lifting, and must cycle on/off without delays. Attach the kit's labels to the back of the listing label plate.
Vent system & damper

Vent with 4" × 6-5/8" coaxial rigid pipe within the master venting chart, starting with an 18" vertical starter made of one 12" and one 6" piece; twist-lock every joint and use no silicone. Then set the vent damper by the flame after 20 minutes, never fully closed on a horizontal termination.

Through the wall

  • With the 18" starter and a 90° elbow, the elbow's horizontal centerline is 53-7/8" above the fireplace floor (add 1/4" rise for every foot of horizontal run). Max horizontal run in that setup: 6".
  • Wall opening 9" wide × 10" high (an 8-inch round hole is acceptable in non-combustible walls). A wall thimble is required in any combustible wall, 4" to 8" thick maximum.
  • Slide the cap over the pipe, screw it to the wall and caulk it. Don't recess the cap into the wall or siding. On vinyl, wood or other combustible siding, use heat shield #AA-11-00458 or an equivalent.
  • Floor-to-vent-cap-centerline figures assume Simpson Duravent GS components; with another brand, measure the parts you're using.

Through the roof

  • Ceiling openings 9" x 9" with a fire stop spacer at each floor; roof opening 9" x 10"; attic insulation shield; support with wall straps every 3 feet.
  • Two vertical caps side by side: 18" between centerlines, and an 18-gauge or heavier galvanized barrier 6" taller and 3" wider than the caps.
Cap height, flat to 6/122 feet
7/12 to 9/122 feet
10/12 to 12/124 feet
13/12 to 16/126 feet
17/12 to 21/128 feet

Exterior cap clearances (from the cap center)

18" above grade, decks and porches, under verandas and balconies, to windows or doors that open, and to soffits (24" to vinyl soffits); 12" to outside and inside corners (vinyl surfaces 24"); 12" to a non-mechanical air supply inlet or another appliance's combustion air inlet; 3 feet to a service regulator vent outlet; never above a meter/regulator assembly within 3 feet horizontally (within a height of 15 feet); 7 feet above a paved public sidewalk or driveway; 24" horizontal to any surface for vertical caps. 18" is recommended to a permanently closed window to prevent condensation. The full lettered list is on p. 35.

Vent damper

Hook the glass latch tool into the end of the damper rod above the glass frame (center of the convection chamber), pull out about 1/8" and turn clockwise to close; a pointer shows the position. If flames ghost off the burners or LP units soot, open it fully and work back in increments.
Gas connection & leak test

Bring the supply in on the left side to the 1/2" N.P.T. female inlet, sized from the pipe table, with a drip leg recommended and CSST on brass-to-brass fittings. Leak-test every field and factory joint with soap solution or a gas sniffer.

Line size from the supply regulator to the factory-installed manual shutoff valve:

Length (feet)Sch. 40 I.D. NG / LP · Type L O.D. NG / LP
0-101/2" / 3/8" · 1/2" / 3/8"
10-401/2" / 1/2" · 5/8" / 1/2"
40-1001/2" / 1/2" · 3/4" / 1/2"
100-1503/4" / 1/2" · 7/8" / 5/8"
150-2003/4" / 1/2" · 7/8" / 3/4"
  • Some areas allow copper tubing or galvanized pipe; never use plastic pipe.
  • Pressure tests above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa): disconnect the appliance and its main gas valve. At or below 1/2 psi: isolate it by closing its shut-off valve.
  • Fit an external keyed wall- or floor-mounted manual shutoff if local code requires one.
  • Check gas leaks and gas pressures before facing materials go on.
Verify orifices, pressure & input

Confirm the stamped orifice sizes (NG #44 rear, #49 front; LP per Fuel & conversion) and set manifold pressure to 3.5" WC +/- 1/8" for NG or 10.0" WC +/- 1/8" for LP. Clock the meter over 30 minutes at maximum flame: the NG input must reach 31,500 Btu below 2000 feet, or 31,000 Btu above.
Electrical & backup inlet

Wire 120 VAC, hot at all times with no switch, into the right-side junction box using the supplied wire nuts and TO HOUSE POWER plug, grounded to code. Mount the DC backup inlet box on the right side within reach of the 6' harness: up to 5 feet away, 18" maximum to the box center.
Liner, logs & glass door

Install the firebox inner liner kit and the chosen log set, coals and inswool media per the instructions supplied with them; logs and coals must not block the pilot or burner flames. Refit the glass door centered in the firebox opening, latch it and check the gasket seal.

Log set options: Norway Spruce, White Oak, Birch or Premium Fiber Oak, each with its own installation instructions. Give the homeowner a copy of the log set instructions.

Door: set the two bottom tabs into the firebox slots, centered left to right; tip the door in until the gasket touches the firebox frame; hook the two top spring latches with the glass latch tool, hook facing down.
Test fire & air shutter

With fresh remote batteries, sync the remote, then confirm the pilot lights immediately and lights both burners, and the flame is stable, not lifting, after 5 minutes. With the logs in, set the air shutters (NG 1/16"-1/8" open, LP 1/4" minimum), trying each setting about ½ hr.

• Don't proceed unless the burner cycles on/off without delays. If flames still lift after 5 minutes, check that every vent pipe is twist-locked and leak proof and the cap is right side up.
  • Front burner shutter: at the gas entry end of the front burner, right side; remove the burner to turn the shutter cap. Rear burner: in the right-side air gap of the glass door frame; put the glass latch tool in the ring terminal and slide forward to open, backward to close.
  • Too blue: close in small 1/8" steps until the flame turns a realistic yellow. Soot on the glass: open fully until it stops, burn four to six hours to clear the deposits, then close in 1/8" steps.
  • LP hint: a good setting gives about a 2" blue base. Yellow flame starting at the burner surface means the shutter is closed too far and will soot.
  • Reference: at maximum height after 30 minutes, a normal rear flame is 1 to 2 inches above the rear log top edge.

Pilot checks: it should light within five to eight seconds of sparking and rectify within five seconds, with flames at least 1" long overlapping the flame sensor and burner ignition ports.
Curing & homeowner handover

Run the 3-step curing cycle before finishing materials go on (blower at level 3 for the first 2 hours), then train the owner and hand over the manual packet. Complete the warranty registration on Mendota's website.

1. Barrier screen, front and doors on. Manual (Off) mode, flame Hi, fan Level 3, at least 2 hours; turn off and cool.
  2. Manual mode, flame Hi, fan Off until curing odors diminish (about 3 hours); leave it on.
  3. Fan to Level 1; keep running until any new odors diminish.

Visible smoke and strong odor are expected, and the smoke will set off smoke alarms; open doors and windows. More than 10 continuous hours on high isn't unusual.

Train the owner on

  • Remote functions, the three thermostat modes, and switching between CPI and IPI
  • Lockout and how to reset it; running on the backup battery system in an outage
  • Master switch location and emergency shutoff; the manual gas shutoff valve with the glass latch tool
  • Removing and refitting the glass door and decorative front; the barrier screen requirement; periodic maintenance

panels.title: Soot on the glass
items: Burner air shutter closed too much → open it fully
Exhaust damper closed too much → open the damper
Glass door seal compromised → gasket corners can't bulge; replace a gasket gone white through the bulb with failed adhesive
Incorrect gas pressure or orifice size → check orifices and outlet pressure (3.5" W.C. NG; 10" W.C. LP)

panels.title: Slow pilot or constant sparking
items: Pilot takes more than ten seconds to light → check spark rod position and igniter wires for pinched or damaged areas
Pilot lit but sparking continues past five seconds → dirty flame sensor; clean it with emery cloth
Still sparking → check the flame sensor lead wire for damage or grounding problems
Frequent lockout → diagnose the cause; never assume the ignition control is faulty

panels.title: Delayed ignition or lifting flames
items: Logs or coals blocking the pilot or main burner flame
Pilot flames under 1" or not overlapping the propagation ports on both burners
Vent pipes not twist-locked or not leak proof
Vent cap not right side up
Slow flame propagation → remove debris and vacuum the burner ports

panels.title: Ghosting flames or recirculation
items: Vent damper closed too far → open it fully, then close back in increments (never fully closed on a horizontal termination)
"Low profile" vent cap → prone to exhaust recirculation and ghosting flames; not allowed
Vertical caps close together → 18" minimum between centerlines and an 18-gauge or heavier galvanized barrier wall between them
Wood-burning flue less than 36" away (centerline to centerline) → metal divider plate recommended, or extend its liner 24" above the top of the gas cap

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself: an igniter sparks the pilot, then the pilot lights the burners. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Before you start

  • Smell all around the fireplace for gas, right down by the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles there.
  • The master switch must be on, or the remote can't talk to the fireplace.
  • Leave the glass door on while the pilot lights. The manual's only exception is the first-time lighting.

Turn it on

  1. Press ON/OFF on the remote. You'll hear a beep, then the igniter starts to spark.
  2. Once the pilot is lit and steady, the gas valve opens and the burners light at full flame.
  3. Adjust the flame with the remote to a level you like.

In a thermostat mode (the remote shows ON or SMART), it only lights if your set temperature is above the room temperature. To turn it off, press ON/OFF.

If the pilot doesn't light, the system locks out. Press ON/OFF to turn it off and reset it, wait five minutes for any gas to clear, then press ON/OFF again. Still locked out? Turn the remote off, on, off, on and off, waiting two seconds between each, then turn it on. If it still won't run, turn off the gas (see Safety) and call your Mendota dealer, service technician or gas supplier.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote comes pre-programmed to your fireplace and takes 3 AAA batteries. Keep it within 20' of the fireplace. Every command gets one beep; no beep, press again.

The buttons

  • On/Off turns the fireplace on or off.
  • Thermostat picks OFF (Manual), ON (Normal Thermostat) or SMART (Smart Thermostat).
  • Mode steps through flame height, fan speed, accent light and rear burner.
  • Up/Down changes the setting on screen: temperature, flame (six levels), fan (six speeds and off), light (six levels) or rear burner on/off.

Thermostat modes

  • Manual burns whatever the room temperature, and shuts off after 24 hours. Don't leave it burning unattended for long periods.
  • Normal turns itself on and off, running until the room is 1°F above your setting.
  • Smart holds your temperature by turning the flame up and down for you.

In both thermostat modes it shuts off after 60 minutes without a remote signal, such as when the remote is in another room or its batteries are weak.

Child lock: press MODE and UP together; repeat to unlock. °F or °C: with the fireplace off, press MODE and Thermostat together.

No beep at all? Re-sync: master switch on, press the sync button once (three beeps), then press ON on the remote within seven seconds (four beeps).

Note: p. 69 puts the master and sync switches in the left side air gap, then the sync switch in the right-side air gap; p. 81 puts both on the right side bottom edge of the glass frame.

sounds.title: Smoke, smell and sounds at first
sounds.html:
A new fireplace has to cure: materials from manufacturing burn off and the powder paint hardens. Some smoke and odor while that happens is normal.

The 3-step curing cycle

Your installer should run this before finishing materials go on around the fireplace. Open doors and windows; the smoke will set off smoke alarms.

  1. With the barrier screen (required) and any front or doors on, run it in Manual (OFF) mode, flame Hi, fan Level 3, for at least 2 hours. The fan keeps the smoke from staining the wall above. Turn it off and let it cool.
  2. Run it again in Manual, flame Hi, fan Off, until the odors fade, about 3 hours. Leave it on.
  3. Set the fan to Level 1. If new odors appear, keep it running until they fade.

It isn't unusual to need more than 10 continuous hours on high before curing odors fade.

Later on

  • Slight odors may come back at startup and fade with use.
  • After three months or more unused, expect a burnt dust and lint smell at first, just like your home heating system in the fall.
  • Noises from the steel expanding and contracting are normal.
A sharp, acrid smell can mean gaps in the glass gasket are leaking exhaust. Ask your service person to check the gasket.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the viewing glass now and then, and only once it has cooled to room temperature.

  • Outside: any glass cleaner you like.
  • Inside: take the glass door off first, then use Kel Kem Polish Plus (part # 65-06-00455) or a comparable product.
  • Never use oven cleaner or abrasive cleaners.
White film? The additives that make gas smell can leave a white film on the glass. Cleaned in a timely manner, it comes off with Polish Plus.

Taking the door off

  1. Use the glass latch tool from your manual packet. Put it in the hole of each of the two top spring latches, pull toward you and turn 90 degrees to release. Leave the hooks upside-down; that makes refitting easier.
  2. With both hands, tip the top of the frame out about 8", lift it up 1" at an angle and move it away.

Putting it back

  1. Set the two bottom tabs into the slots at the bottom of the firebox, centered left to right.
  2. Tip the door in until the gasket touches the firebox frame.
  3. Hook each spring latch back on with the tool, hook facing down.
Check the gasket every time the door comes off. Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken; replacing glass is a job for a licensed or qualified person.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI and CPI
modes.html:
Your fireplace lights a small pilot flame first, then uses it to light the burners. You choose how long the pilot stays lit.

IPIpilot lights only when you call for heat, and stays on only while the burners run
CPIpilot stays lit, and shuts off after 7 days without use

Each time you use the fireplace, the 7-day clock starts over. A snowflake icon shows on the remote whenever CPI is on. The manual also calls CPI "Pilot on Demand" and "Standing Pilot Mode".

To switch

With the remote off, press MODE; the screen shows CPI or IPI. Press Up for CPI or Down for IPI, then press ON/OFF to start the fireplace.

Why CPI in winter

A lit pilot keeps the chimney warm for a strong draft at startup, cuts condensation on the glass, keeps the firebox warm against cold drafts and heat loss, and helps prevent lockouts.

Note: p. 10 says CPI is required in winter when outside daily highs stay at 50°F or lower; p. 73 says Mendota recommends CPI when the average daily high falls below 50°F.

At flame level 1, pressing Down turns all the burners off. In IPI the pilot goes out too; in CPI it stays lit.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
Day to day, the fireplace runs on house power. Its supply stays on at all times, with no wall switch.

During a power outage

  1. Get the backup battery pack (a holder with 4 AA batteries) and its harness from your manual packet.
  2. Plug the pack (6V DC maximum, supplied with your fireplace) into the backup power inlet port your installer mounted to the right of the fireplace.
  3. Use the remote as usual.

On battery, the burner and flame height work. The fan and accent light don't.

Keep the pack and harness somewhere safe and easy to find, so they're ready when the power goes out.

Remote batteries

  • The remote takes 3 AAA batteries. Change them at least every 6 months, or more often if you use the fireplace a lot.
  • A battery icon appears on the remote's screen when they're low.
  • Very weak batteries can make the fireplace shut off in a thermostat mode.
TV heat kits: if a Versiheat or FlexHeat system was installed so a TV can hang above, the fireplace can't be run during a power outage.

flames.title: Flames & soot
flames.html:
After 30 minutes or more at full height, a normal rear flame reaches 1 to 2 inches above the top edge of the rear log. Your gas type, air shutter setting and vent setup can make it slightly higher or lower.

The air shutters, damper, coals and embers are set for your fuel and venting by a qualified technician. If you think it isn't burning right, contact your installer or Mendota dealer. Improper setup and adjustment isn't covered by the warranty.

Want less heat?

Turn off the rear burner and lower the flame from the remote. Turn the fan down or off to spread less heat.

Soot

A few small soot spots on the logs are acceptable.

Turn it off and tell your Mendota dealer right away if you see soot areas larger than 1"x1" on the logs, a thin black film on the glass, or soot on the outside of your home around the vent cap. Mendota and its dealers aren't responsible for damage from sooting that wasn't reported right away.

Carbon deposits on the logs also mean: turn it off and call a qualified installer, service agency or your gas supplier.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any light switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions.
  • If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.

Shutting it down

In an emergency, flip the master switch to off and the main burners shut off; your installer should show you where it is. To turn off the gas: press ON/OFF on the remote, turn off CPI pilot mode, then close the manual shutoff valve in the left air gap, next to the glass frame, by turning the glass latch tool 90 degrees counterclockwise. Close any outside shutoff valve too. If service is to be performed, turn off all electric power to the fireplace.

Hot surfaces and children

  • The barrier screen must be on whenever the fireplace runs. If it's damaged, replace it.
  • Keep furniture and other objects at least 60" from the front of the barrier screen, and nothing on the front edge of the mantel.
  • The glass and the surfaces around it can be too hot to touch. That's normal, but supervise children and pets; a safety gate is recommended for anyone at risk.
  • In a bedroom, study or other isolated room, always use a thermostat mode, never Manual.
Never burn wood or paper in it, and don't use it if any part has been under water. Mendota requires replacing the entire appliance if any portion has been submerged.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
Have a qualified installer, service agency or your gas supplier service the fireplace at least once a year, in the summer or early fall.

What the visit covers

  • Cleaning lint and dust around the control and blower, and checking the wiring under the burner
  • Cleaning the pilot flame sensor and sparker rods, and vacuuming the pilot
  • Checking the pilot and burner flames
  • Vacuuming the burner ports; the manual notes that mercaptan in natural gas attracts nesting insects
  • Removing and cleaning the logs and coals, and checking them for carbon
  • Checking the glass door gasket, and replacing it if it has turned white through and its adhesive has failed
  • Clearing debris from the vent cap, and cleaning the glass and any enamel lining

Your part

  • Look at the outside vent cap every month for anything blocking the airflow.
  • Change the remote batteries at least every 6 months.
  • Keep the area around it clear of anything that can burn. Lint from carpet and bedding can mean more frequent cleaning.
Under the warranty, annual maintenance is the original purchaser's job, and problems caused by a lack of maintenance can void it.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Mendota gives a limited lifetime warranty to the original purchaser, as long as the fireplace stays where it was first installed. It can't be transferred.

  • Coverage starts on the date Mendota invoiced your installing dealer, and applies only to new units sold through an authorized Mendota dealer.
  • Which parts are covered, and for how long, is set out in a table on p. 87 that this guide can't reproduce. Check the PDF or ask your dealer.
  • It requires installation by a dealer-approved installer with proper permits and inspections, and problems caused by skipped yearly maintenance can void it.

Not covered, for example

  • Water damage, and rust or corrosion from a lack of maintenance or improper venting
  • Door and glass gasketing, discoloration and minor warping
  • Over-firing, misuse, improper installation, or damage in transit
  • Noises from the steel expanding and contracting

Making a claim

Report the problem to your Mendota dealer within 30 days, with proof of purchase, the purchase date, model name and serial number. The model and serial number are on the listing label, which hangs on a cable in the air gap and pulls out for reading.

Parts you buy after the coverage ends carry a 90-day warranty with a receipt, with no labor.

specInput.html:

Input rate verification (NG)

Turn off all other appliances and their pilots, read the meter, run 30 minutes at maximum flame, read it again. (Final − initial therms) × 100,000 × 2 must be at least 31,500 Btu below 2000 feet, or at least 31,000 Btu above 2000 feet.

  • Never over- or under-fire by changing orifice sizes or adjusting gas pressure above nameplate.
  • Backyard natural gas well: submit gas analysis data sheets to Mendota for orifice sizing before first firing. Unpurified gas voids the warranty.
  • Above 7,500 ft: check derating with the local gas company or Mendota Technical Service. When de-rating, fill in the High Altitude De-Rating Label (owner's manual packet) and fix it to the back of the listing label plate.

Never adjust gas pressure to raise the input above the nameplate. Over-firing can permanently damage the firebox and voids the warranty.

specVent.html:

  • No silicone at pipe joints (stove gasket cement allowed, not required). No "low profile" vent caps.
  • Twist-lock every joint; use fixed lengths rather than telescoping sections where possible.
  • Horizontal runs level or 1/4" rise per foot toward the cap, never downward; support every 3 ft.
  • Never connect to a chimney serving another appliance; no common vents.
  • Dual, triple and four-elbow layouts have their own tables (pp. 59 and 62). Above 7500 ft, ask Mendota technical service.

Power vent: total vent length 1' to 80' with up to 6 90° elbows; kit AA-11-04071 for horizontal runs under 25 feet, AA-11-04072 over 25 feet, AA-11-04100 for vertical.

Note: on how elbows count toward 40 feet, p. 56 says to add only the lengths of the straight pipe sections; p. 58 says the total of all pipe sections includes the restriction of elbows.
Note: for four 90° elbows (vertical termination), p. 62 requires a minimum 18 inches of vertical starter in Prerequisite #2, while its table heads the starter column V1 (3' MIN.).

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Unit to floor0 in.
Unit to enclosure sidewall / back wall1/2 in.
Top standoffs (Figure 3-8)0"
Unit bottom to enclosure ceiling60 3/16 in.
Unit bottom to room ceiling72 in.
Glass edge to adjacent sidewall16 in.
8" mantel above top convection air opening20 in.
Vent pipe top / bottom / sides3 in. / 1 in. / 1 in.
Furniture and objects in front60" from the barrier screen

Side walls (p. 21)

Combustible walls, mantel legs and corbels must stay behind a 45-degree line from the side edges of the visible glass unless they're more than 16" away. Where 16" can't be met: a 20-gauge or heavier steel shield on 1" standoffs (open top and bottom, 12" larger each way than the heat source) cuts it 66% to 5-3/8"; R-1 ceramic or mineral board cuts it 50% to 8".

Mantels (p. 22)

The top of the convection air opening is 28-5/8" above the fireplace floor. The 12" above it is a non-combustible zone, so a combustible mantel can start at 40-5/8" and then grow 1:1 in depth with height: an 8" deep mantel at 48-5/8" minimum; a 12" mantel 24" above the convection air opening.

Finishing (pp. 25-28)

  • Non-combustible zones need materials rated per NFPA 220 or passing ASTM E 136. Paper-faced drywall (including Type X) and WonderBoard are not approved there.
  • Finishing guides protrude 1"; a wall finish at least 1" deep is recommended. Finish over 2 ½" deep needs the Recessed Mount guide kit.
  • Facings directly outside the top convection air gap can reach 350 °F.
  • Smooth walls: fasten board to the framing and float it over the face, not screwed to the fireplace, with no seams above it.

TV above (recommendations): a mantel at least 2" deeper than the TV with its top 12" above the top air gap (if the mantel is combustible, make certain the entire mantel meets the combustible mantel clearances above); or a recessed cavity starting 16" above it; or a Cool Wall, two Versiheat fans or FlexHeat system (TV 12" above the top air gap, convection fans off). Corner installation dimensions are shown only as a diagram (Figure 3-4, p. 17).

specFraming.title: Framing & hearth
specFraming.html:
Rough framing width40-5/8"
Rough framing height40-3/4"
Rough framing depth14-5/8"
Maker's website: Minimum Fireplace Framing Requirements: Front Width 39 1/2", Rear Width 40 5/8", Depth 14 5/8", Height 40 3/4". The manual gives one framing width, 40-5/8". Install to the manual.
Vent opening height × width10" × 9"
Unit (Figure 3-5)40 7/16" H × 39 7/16" W × 14 9/16" D
Finishing guide (Figure 3-5)32 5/8" W × 27 1/16" H
Glass frame (Figure 3-5)31 1/2" W × 26 3/8" H
Maker's website: Viewing Area 32 5/8" x 27 1/16". The manual gives no viewing area; Figure 3-5 gives these figures as the finishing guide width and height.
Net weight220 lbs. (team lift recommended)

On the left side, the ignition system box protrudes ½" and an electrical cable clamp 1-1/4". If the unit is recessed deeper than 14-5/8", everything protruding past its front face must be non-combustible.

Floor & hearth pad

  • Set it on a wood, masonry or metal floor running its full width and depth; never directly on carpet, vinyl or any combustible other than wood. No R-1 rating is needed under the fireplace.
  • Sitting on the floor, it needs a non-combustible R-1 hearth protector at least 18" deep in front; p. 12 gives the pad as 1-1/2" thick maximum.
  • Each 1" the fireplace is raised cuts that depth by 2"; raised 6" or more, no R-1 hearth protector is required. The floor in front can still reach 200 °F; with carpet, vinyl or laminate, raising it at least 12" is recommended.
  • The factory bottom guide sits 1 1/2" ("A") above the bottom of the fireplace. Cover that band with a hearth pad built level with the guide, or with non-combustible wall finish if the unit is raised above the pad. A pad thicker than "A" means raising the unit: a 4" pad, 2 1/2".

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Ratings information120 Volts AC, 1.5 Amps (minimum line voltage allowed 110 Volts AC)
AC power requirements120 VAC, 2 Amp power or a 6V DC power source
Backupbattery holder with 4 AA (6V DC maximum)
Remote3 AAA
Note: the manual gives the current rating as 1.5 Amps in the ratings information on p. 15 and as 2 Amp in the AC power requirements on p. 37.
  • The AC supply must be hot at all times, with no switch in it.
  • Junction box on the right side, reached through the blower and control module access panel. Route the house cable through the strain relief in the cover plate, join each wire to the matching colored wire with the supplied wire nuts, and plug the TO HOUSE POWER plug (manual packet) into the plug toward the front; the plugs only fit one way.
  • Braided to braided: strip both ends ½" and twist before the wire nut. Braided to solid: strip solid ½", braided ¾", and twist the braided around the solid.
  • Ground per local codes, or NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1. Mobile homes: bolt the unit to the floor and ground it.

DC backup inlet

Install the supplied 6' harness, single gang box and cover plate on the right side, up to 5 feet from the unit, at a maximum height of 18" to the box center (or matching the room's other outlets). Don't staple the harness to the studs. Fit the white or beige cover plate and the notification decal, then show the homeowner how to connect the backup pack.

specFuel.title: Fuel & LP conversion
specFuel.html:
Ships configured for natural gas. To burn LP, a qualified service agency installs LP gas conversion kit #HA-106-00023: one motorized LP pressure regulator #907.012, two cap orifices #65-14-00364 (drill #3/64") and an L-shaped Torx wrench.

Orifice sizes (ratings information)

0-2000ft, rear burner#44 NG · 3/64" LP
0-2000ft, front burner#49 NG · 3/64" LP
2000-4500ft, rear burner#44 NG · 3/64" LP
2000-4500ft, front burner#49 NG · #55 LP
Note: for the LP orifices at 2000-4500 ft, the ratings information gives 3/64" rear and #55 front on p. 15; the high-altitude section gives #55 rear and 3/64" front on p. 44; the LPG input-rate section on p. 44 says 3/64" rear and front for all elevations, and the kit on p. 49 contains two 3/64" orifices.

Air shutter

Natural gas1/16"-1/8" open
L.P. gas1/4" minimum open

For altitudes above 4,500', some variations may be required. After converting, attach the kit's labels, and any filled-in high-altitude label, to the back of the listing label plate.

index_extra.p: What to do if you smell gas
Lockout: wait five minutes, then reset from the remote
Master switch on, sync button, then ON within seven seconds
CPI keeps the pilot lit until 7 days without use
Plug in the backup battery pack; burner works, fan doesn't
Mantel, recessed cavity or a heat transfer system

conflicts.issue: Current rating: ratings information says '120 Volts AC, 1.5 Amps (minimum line voltage allowed 110 Volts AC)'; AC Power Requirements says '120 VAC, 2 Amp power or a 6V DC power source'.

LP orifices at 2000-4500 ft: ratings information gives rear 3/64" LP and front #55 LP; High Altitude De-Rating text gives Propane #55 (Rear) and 3/64" (Front); LPG Input Rate Verification says 3/64" rear and front 'for all elevations'; the conversion kit lists only two 3/64" cap orifices.

Master/sync switch location: p. 69 note says 'bottom left corner of the fireplace in the left side air gap', p. 69 step 2 says the sync switch is 'above master switch in the right-side air gap', and p. 81 says both are 'mounted on the right side bottom edge of the glass frame'.

Winter pilot mode: 'It is required to activate the Standing Pilot Mode ... when outside daily high temperatures remain 50oF or lower' (p. 10) vs 'Mendota recommends that CPI mode is used during the winter months when the average daily high temperature falls below 50°F' (p. 73); the p. 86 checklist says CPI 'is suggested during cold season'.

Counting toward the 40 ft vent system length: p. 56 says add the lengths of the straight pipe sections only; p. 58 says 'Combined total length of all pipe sections (include restriction of elbows) ... shall be less than 40 feet'.
Four 90-degree elbows, vertical termination: Prerequisite #2 requires 'a minimum 18 inches of vertical starter section', while the table on the same page heads the column 'V1(3' MIN.)'.

catalog_mismatches.manual: Unit height 40 7/16 (Figure 3-5 label); 40-3/4" is the minimum rough framing height (pp. 15, 20)
Unit depth 14 9/16 (Figure 3-5 label); 14-5/8" is the minimum rough framing depth (pp. 15, 20)
No viewing area is stated. 32 5/8 and 27 1/16 are the finishing guide width and height in Figure 3-5; the glass frame itself is 31 1/2 wide x 26 3/8 high
Minimum rough framing width 40-5/8" (pp. 15, 20), with no separate front width; unit width 39 7/16 (Figure 3-5, p. 18)

review.notes: One manual (85-03-01106 rev. R, 92 pp.); p. 91 is blank. Warranty coverage periods are in a table on p. 87 that has no text, so the guide only points to it. No code table in the manual (beeps for sync are described in the remote drawer), so codes is empty. Figure text used only where the label sits with its value: unit 40 7/16 H x 39 7/16 W x 14 9/16 D (Fig. 3-5, p. 18) and '0" clearance from top standoffs' (Fig. 3-8, p. 21). Not used: Figures 3-3/3-4 on p. 17 print a second set of values ('minimum rough framing dimensions' 47" / 42-1/2" / 19-1/2", 50" unit base to enclosure ceiling, 48" min. to 8" mantel) that can't be tied to a configuration and differ from the ratings table (40-3/4" framing height, 60 3/16 in. enclosure ceiling, 48-5/8" mantel); Fig. 3-9 on p. 21 shows a '36 3/4" rough framing height'; corner installation is pointed to as a diagram. Exterior cap clearances on p. 35: letters and values are split in the text, so the guide lists only clearances whose description and value sit together and leaves out the mechanical air supply inlet, whose value is printed apart from its description. Also not used: the LP pilot orifice '#977.168' and regulator range '[10.0-5.5"WC]' printed in Figure 4-4 (the kit parts list and pilot procedure don't use them); metric equivalents (p. 15 gives 40-3/4" as 94 cm). Smaller wording issues left unflagged: thermostat-mode fan runs 12-1/2 minutes after the flames (p. 70) vs 12 minutes (p. 86), so the guide gives no number; p. 12 says the R-1 hearth pad is '1-1/2" Thick Maximum' while p. 24 shows a 4" pad with the unit raised 2 1/2" (both shown in specFraming); listing label is 'in the air gap below the Fireplace' (p. 13), 'below the bottom edge of the glass door frame' (p. 75) and 'in the air gap on the side' (p. 44), so the guide only says it hangs in the air gap; p. 58 allows three 90-degree elbows with 25 ft horizontal without the 3 ft-per-elbow deduction given on pp. 55-56 (guide shows the deduction); the manual says not to use a 1-piece 18" starter yet gives a 1-3/8" higher wall hole for one (pp. 33, 55, 57); Micore 1/2" board R-value 1.27-1.47 (p. 23) vs 1.2-1.4 (p. 25), not shown; 110 VAC (pp. 18, 76) vs 120 VAC elsewhere (p. 15 gives 110 V as the minimum line voltage); 'AUX On' not used on this fireplace (p. 71) vs Auxiliary turning heat transfer kits on/off (p. 72), neither used; the gas inlet is a 1/2" female NPT (pp. 41, 43) while p. 43 also mentions connecting to a '1/2" male NPT flex end adapter'; the p. 45 checklist places LP conversion after the unit is in the chase while p. 50 recommends converting before (step order follows the checklist; the step text gives the recommendation); the p. 45 checklist says to install the accent light bulb and lens while p. 48 says they come installed; the p. 86 checklist carries 'INSERTS ONLY' and '(ProFlame units only)' lines. Catalog checks that match: BTU NG 31,500/8,965 and LP 31,500/12,627, efficiency 74.5% (manual labels it 'P.4', catalog basis 'P.4.1'), vent 4 x 6-5/8, weight 220 lbs, 95 CFM blower standard, IPI ignition, ANSI Z21.88/CSA 2.33, manufactured-home approval, model AA-11-03055. Catalog width 39.5 is the website's 'Minimum Fireplace Framing Requirements: Front Width 39 1/2"'; the manual's only framing width is 40-5/8" (in catalog_mismatches). The website's framing height 40 3/4" and depth 14 5/8" match the manual's rough framing figures, and its 'CSA P.4.1 Efficiency 74.5%' matches the manual's P.4 74.5%.
